Let me analyze this conflict.

The register says applicant: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."
The document says: "MINEBEA CO., LTD."

These are genuinely different company names. Minebea Co., Ltd. is the former name of MinebeaMitsumi Inc. — the company renamed in 2017 after merging with Mitsumi Electric. However, the certificate is from 2012 (issuing_year: 2012), so at the time of issuance, the legal entity was Minebea Co., Ltd.

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is this "legal-suffix drift"? No — "Mitsumi" is not a legal suffix; it's part of a different company name entirely. MinebeaMitsumi Inc. vs Minebea Co., Ltd. are different legal names (the former resulted from a 2017 merger/rename). So this is different-entity.

However, one could argue they are the same corporate entity that renamed. But the rules as given: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. This is more than that — the company name changed due to merger. From a data fusion standpoint, the certificate is the legal instrument, and at the time the certificate was issued, the applicant was Minebea Co., Ltd. The register's "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." might reflect a later-updated registrant name. But following the given rules strictly: genuinely different company names = different-entity, best_value = document's.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value: "MINEBEA CO., LTD." with a short why sentence.
